subjective: The pet parent reports that the female cat had ringworm, which has resolved after topical medication. The male cat is undergoing treatment again and has recovered. The female cat is four months old. The pet parent inquires about vaccination status and confirms that the male cat has received his first rabies vaccine. The pet parent notes some concern about breathing appearing reduced during motion, but the veterinarian clarifies this is not an actual reduction. The cat has been laxed for one week. There is mention of possible gas-related issues and monitoring for bloat.
objective: The veterinarian confirms that the ringworm infection in the female cat is resolved following topical treatment. The male cat has received the first rabies vaccination. No current signs of bloat are observed. The cat's breathing appears normal on examination, with no actual reduction noted. No additional physical examination details or vital signs were provided.
assessment: Resolved ringworm infection in the female cat following topical treatment. Male cat is up to date with first rabies vaccination. Possible gastrointestinal gas issues are being monitored. No evidence of bloat at this time. Continued observation recommended.
plan: Continue monitoring the cats at home. No further immediate treatment for ringworm is needed unless symptoms recur, in which case oral medication may be considered. The male cat will require booster rabies vaccinations in the future, which can be administered at the hospital. Monitor for any signs of bloat or worsening gastrointestinal symptoms; if these occur, diagnostic imaging such as ultrasound may be warranted. Owner advised to observe breathing and activity levels and report any changes.
conclusion: The female cat had ringworm which has resolved with topical treatment. The male cat has received his first rabies vaccination and will require booster doses later. There is no current evidence of bloat or respiratory compromise, though the pet parent noted apparent reduced breathing during motion which was not confirmed on examination. The cats are being monitored for gastrointestinal gas issues. The plan includes continued observation, possible oral medication for ringworm if needed, and future booster vaccinations for the male cat. Owner instructions include monitoring for any changes and seeking veterinary care if symptoms worsen.
key_issues:
1. Ringworm infection in female cat - resolved with topical treatment; monitoring for recurrence.
2. Vaccination status of male cat - first rabies vaccine administered; booster doses pending.
3. Gastrointestinal gas issues - currently monitored; no bloat detected.
4. Respiratory concerns - apparent reduced breathing during motion not confirmed on exam.
abnormal_findings: No abnormal findings reported. Ringworm resolved. No bloat or respiratory compromise detected.
customer_instructions: Monitor the cats at home for any recurrence of ringworm or gastrointestinal symptoms. Observe breathing and activity levels. Bring the male cat to the hospital for booster rabies vaccinations as scheduled. Seek veterinary care if any signs of bloat, worsening breathing, or other concerning symptoms develop.
reminders: Schedule booster rabies vaccination for the male cat at the hospital. Monitor for signs of bloat or respiratory distress and return for evaluation if symptoms develop or worsen.
